quotes.text: governance isn't technology, governance is structure. It's the deliberate choices you make about ownership, accountability and how information flows. Those choices have to come first. The tool is the byproduct.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the episode's core argument that structure must precede tooling.

quotes.text: The moment you decide to catalog everything you've already failed, not because you didn't work hard enough, but because of your intent you chose to build for completeness, instead of building for a person
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why big-bang cataloging fails compared to use case first.

quotes.text: A reader sees metadata, not the actual data. They see table names, column descriptions, owners and lineage. They see the structure, but they never see customer records or financial details.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clears up the common fear behind overly restrictive catalog read access.

quotes.text: The purview administrator group sits empty by default. No one is an active member. Users are made eligible. Eligibility means they can request activation, but they don't have the power until they actually activated.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Describes a concrete just-in-time model for the most powerful Purview role.

quotes.text: The moment you write ownership explicitly at each layer, the medallion architecture stops being just a storage pattern. It becomes an accountability chain.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes the medallion architecture as an ownership model, not just storage.

takeaways: Start a Microsoft Purview rollout with one concrete business question instead of scanning and cataloging everything.
Purview access spans four layers (tenant, data map, unified catalog, governance domain), so bundle each persona's permissions into about five role groups assigned to Entra groups.
Protect the Purview administrator role with just-in-time PIM activation and make ownership explicit for every data product and medallion layer.
hook: Microsoft Purview is already in your tenant, and that ease is exactly why so many data governance rollouts end in permission sprawl and an unused catalog. This episode shows data governance and platform teams how to roll out Purview use case first, with a four-layer permission blueprint, role groups, data products and PIM-protected admins.
